steps.title: Set Up Google Cloud Project
steps.detail: Create a Google Cloud project, verify your domain, and enable the Gmail API. Ensure the project meets the domain verification requirement (claim f26).

steps.title: Create OAuth Credentials
steps.detail: In the Google Cloud Console, navigate to APIs & Services → Credentials, create a new OAuth 2.0 client ID of type "Web application". Note the client ID and client secret (claim f13).

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs
steps.detail: Add the Composio callback URL shown in the Composio dashboard to the "Authorized redirect URIs" list. Verify that the URI matches exactly (claims f14, f15).

steps.title: Link OAuth Credentials to Composio
steps.detail: In Composio’s Gmail Toolkit settings, paste the client ID and client secret, and set the scopes to gmail.send and gmail.modify. Confirm that the Composio-managed auth flow uses PKCE with S256 (claim p1).

steps.title: Test Authorization Flow
steps.detail: Using the Composio dashboard, initiate a test authorization. Verify that users can log in to Google, consent to the requested scopes, and that tokens are received. Ensure redirect works correctly (claims f9, f10, f11).

steps.title: Submit for Google Review
steps.detail: Prepare the required documentation: brand verification (claim f25), domain verification (claim f26), privacy policy, and demo video if required (claim f8). Submit the OAuth client for scope verification of gmail.send (claim f18) and security assessment (claim f23).

steps.title: Google Review Period
steps.detail: During the review, keep the Composio managed auth operational and monitor the status. If reviewers flag issues, update the privacy policy or brand information as requested.

steps.title: Enable Production Access
steps.detail: Once the review approves, set production_access_review to yes and verify the app functions for users outside your org. Test the full send & manage flow.

whileYouWait.text: Keep using the Composio-managed auth for internal testing to ensure the flow remains functional during the review.
Add or update demo video and privacy policy in the Google Cloud Console as needed based on reviewer feedback.

gotchas.text: Scope verification for gmail.send can take several weeks; plan release accordingly.
Brand verification may flag your public homepage or privacy policy, causing review delays.
Google no longer supports less‑secure apps; ensure all connections use OAuth.

claims.text: Google has deprecated the IAP OAuth Admin API, requiring migration to Google‑managed OAuth clients.

sources.quote: The Identity‑Aware Proxy (IAP) OAuth Admin API is now deprecated...IAP now uses a Google‑managed OAuth client for browser access by default...

claims.text: Google will no longer support less‑secure apps and Google Sync from March 14, 2025, requiring OAuth for Gmail access.

sources.quote: Starting March 14, 2025, you and your users must use OAuth with third‑party apps to access Gmail...Google is turning off access to less secure apps.

claims.text: Apps accessing Google user data via server must undergo annual security assessment after brand verification.

sources.quote: If the app accesses or has the capability to access Google user data from or through a server...the system must undergo an annual security assessment.

claims.text: Sensitive scope verification process can take several weeks and follows brand verification which takes 2‑3 business days.

sources.quote: The automated review usually completes in a few minutes...restricted scopes verification process can potentially take several weeks to complete.

verifier.note: Quote not found on the page; Quote states the automated review is quick but restricted scopes can take weeks; does not specify 2‑3 business days for brand verification.

claims.text: Automation scripts using the IAP OAuth Admin API must be updated to stop calling the deprecated API.

sources.quote: If your automation scripts or Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools use the IAP OAuth 2.0 Admin API...you must update the scripts so that they don't use the IAP OAuth 2.0 Admin API.

claims.text: OAuth apps with branding changes must first complete brand verification before scope verification can proceed.

sources.quote: Note that all apps must complete the brand verification step first, which typically takes 2-3 business days...

claims.text: OAuth app reviews can stall for weeks, especially if the brand verification incorrectly flags public homepage or privacy policy.

sources.quote: OAuth brand verification incorrectly flagging public homepage and privacy policy before production deadline

verifier.note: Quote mentions brand verification issues but does not quantify the stall duration.
